what: Installed with nothing that uses it: no view and no status bar entry, and one notice naming the extensions that use it, with a button to install each
On a first install with an extension that uses it, one notice asking for a token mode, whose button opens the list of modes

VS Code's webview request limit: asked about once per VS Code build while agentPlus.webviewRequestLimit is ask, raised to 1000000 in VS Code's service-worker.js when chosen, raised without asking while the setting is raise (except on Linux), left alone while it is leave, and put back to 32 by its command

The Conversations view in the panel: one row per running conversation of this workspace with its state, questions and open rows, stopped ones with open rows under a group of their own, and a warning row when an agent could not list its conversations
The icon of each conversation's row by its activity: a green dot while a turn runs, a green ring while only background work runs, red while it waits for the user, and none once it has stopped
The envelope at the end of a conversation's row while it has a reply not seen, shown also on a row with a dot; it goes once the conversation is opened, and a row with nothing new never has one
The envelope at the end of a row with a reply not read: 📩 in a dark theme, and the plain envelope's text form in the Light Modern and High Contrast Light themes, clear on each background
A long title cut short in a narrow Conversations view, with the envelope after it still whole at the row's end

A plan question waiting on the user under its conversation's row, with how long ago it was asked; one asked after the user's last message turns the conversation red, an older one does not; the view's badge counts the questions and the status bar entry the conversations that have one, on a red background

The Answer view beside Conversations: a click on a question shows it with its row and a box to answer in; Send hands the answer to the window showing the conversation and says whether it was sent, left in the conversation's input box, or not received

A click on a conversation whose agent keeps a brief shows that brief in the Answer view: its summary and where it stands, when each was written and whether it may be out of date, or a brief put together from the plan and marked as such; its button and the row's arrow go to the conversation
A doing row under a conversation, which goes to that conversation when clicked

The Work plan view in the Agent Plus sidebar: the plan of the conversation in front, following its tab, with the agent's name, a badge counting its open rows, a hover on each row with its question, and the welcome text for a tab with no conversation yet
A click on a plan row opens a dialog with its description, state, question and place in the plan
Open the Work Plan File in the view's title bar and on a row's right-click menu, and Refresh, which reads every plan afresh

For an extension that draws a plan bar above its agent's input box: planSummary giving a conversation's plan in the bar's figures and onDidChangePlanSummary firing when it changes, agentPlus.showWorkPlanOf moving the Work plan view to a conversation, and agentPlus.answerQuestionOf showing its first question in the Answer view
A row above the plan that the conversation's agent puts there, for example when its work plan plugin is not installed, and that runs the agent's command when clicked
A row in a state this version does not know, a plan in a newer format, and a plan that does not parse, each marked as such
The Conversations button in the Work plan view's title bar, and the status bar entry, N conversations need you (listed when you hover over it) or Conversations M, both showing the Conversations view
With more than one agent registered, each conversation's row drawn with its agent's logo and the activity dot on it

A notification in the focused window when a conversation starts to wait, or stops with a reply not read and stays stopped for 5 seconds; none when only an envelope appears, none for a turn followed at once by another, and none for the conversation in front
Open on a notification bringing its conversation to the front, and two conversations that start to wait together getting one notification each, whose Open brings that conversation to the front

The Conversations entry in the status bar counting the conversations that wait or stopped with a reply not read, less the one in front, which falls by one when one is read, and Show the Conversations That Need You listing them to open one
agentPlus.notifications.waiting and .finished each turning off their kind of notification, and agentPlus.notifications.enabled turning off the notifications and the count

The token mode entry in the status bar: its short name, a hover saying what the mode adds to the agent's context, and a click listing the four modes. Each of Interface, Essential, All and Custom can be chosen there, and Custom opens the Settings editor on the features' own settings
agentPlus.workPlanView hiding the Work plan view, and agentPlus.conversationsView hiding the Conversations and Answer views and the Conversations status bar entry
Show Status writing the version, the extensions using Agent Plus, the token mode and every registered agent to the Agent Plus output
Open on a notification, or a row, for a conversation another VS Code window shows: that window takes the request, shows the conversation and comes to the front
notInWindow: Each test window has a user data folder of its own, and the window that takes the request comes to the front through VS Code's command line, which knows only the default one: it would start a second VS Code on that profile instead of bringing the test window forward. test/parts/46-window-open.js covers the request, the reveal and which command line is run.

what: In Restricted Mode the views still draw, and the Answer view says it sends no answer
